item.title: [REDACTED] The Musical!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch: whenever the SCP is used, anyone that hears the tuning will immediately break into a song and dance number akin to that of a Broadway performance.

Central Narrative: none

Hook/Attention-Grabber: this SCP causes anyone who hears it to break into song and dance, and anyone who hears someone singing while under this affect will become part of the performance. While under this effect subjects with terrible singing voices will suddenly gain perfect pitch, people who can't dance or are out of shape will suddenly be able to perform movements and gymnastic techniques that would require years of training and months of intense choreography to perform, subjects with no instrument playing experience will suddenly be able to play musical instruments at an expert level. No one will realize this effect is happening until the performance is over.

Additional Notes:I'm not sure if this SCP would be classified as a joke SCP or just a funny SCP. there's also going to be a list of songs created by this SCP which are mostly SCP parodies of famous musical songs, such as;

  • It's a D-Class life (It's a hard knock life from Annie)
  • Defying Human Rights (Defying Gravity from Wicked)
  • Send in the Keter (Send in the Clowns from A Little Night Music)
  • The Sound of Science (The Sound of Music)
  • Ya Got a Breach (Ya Got Trouble from The Music Man)
  • If I were an O5 (If I were a Rich Man from Fiddler on the Roof)

and I just want to make sure, would I also need to include lyrics for these songs, I'm pretty sure I would, but I just want to be sure.

The difference, to me, is a requirement versus a consequence. A cognitohazard could spread and we could harvest a tremendous amount of information about what happens as a result, and then "be ignorant" of the cognitohazard while keeping the adjacent information.

In the scenario I've constructed, containment requires rejecting that sort of information.


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: Dr. Eates Proposal

I'm deeply frustrated that the entire article ends up being the backstory for a one-off esoteric object class that SCP-1055 proves can be handled just fine by Keter. The voting protocol is a fantastic way to open the article, the containment procedures prime me for a potentially interesting spin on antimemetics, and the O5 Council simply not existing at all is a hell of a hook… and then nothing is done with that hook.

None of the O5 Council's spooky missives have weight because they aren't being associated with any actions of consequence. The letters from each administrator to their successor similarly lack weight because we don't know what kind of evil each one was complicit in or what regrets they have in complying with the Council. The Pripyat Incident might be Chernobyl but I don't know because there's no context for any of these actions or decisions. The O5 Meeting Minutes are similarly inconsequential because it's just vaguely spooky sounding dialogue that doesn't build up to anything.

The O5 correspondence with Michelle is the most promising part of this article. Despite the complete lack of buildup to this point, I still felt some catharsis when she defied them and passed the test. And then that catharsis was deflated utterly when she used her newfound freedom and authority to… create and define a new one-off object class.

The article clearly wants to be a meditation on the struggle of holding to one's ideals and morals in the face of authoritarian and institutional pressure, but it doesn't demonstrate that challenge effectively. Show us what crises the previous Administrators faced and how the Council ground them down. Show us how powerful the idea of the Council is and demonstrate Michelle's moral fortitude through more than just back-and-forth emails. I understand that the object class is supposed to be used to justify why there's so little documentation and context for this article, but it would be just as easy to say that the "Atelis Protocol" mandates these infosecurity requirements without wasting so much time reminding us that this thing has an esoteric object class. Forget the esoteric object class and focus on the power struggle.


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: Dr. Eates Proposal

This is competently executed, but there's nothing particularly compelling that I feel like I haven't seen before. "[Foundation thing] is anomalously fake" and "spooky people talking gibberish mysteriously" are both pretty well-worn tropes, and aside from the presentation of a quasi-feral O5 council, there wasn't much that really caught my eye.

Ending it on the justification for why this needed a new object class soured it for me, so I gotta -1 it.

item.title: Re: SCP Draft: Extra-Dimensional Vacuum Cleaner
item.content:encoded:
Hello! To start off, I am not on the butterfly roster so take this with grain of salt.

Crit
Hide crit

Upon opening your article I immediately noticed some formatting issues. "Item #:" should be bolded, it looks like you forgot to put the closing asterisks. The "Item #:" field should only contain the designation number, not the actual name of your SCP.

For your containment procedures, you don't need to state things that are already the "normal thing to do". Specifically:

The closet is to be locked at all times unless SCP-XXXX is currently undergoing testing

This is already implied. You can reword this to "Access to SCP-XXXX is strictly limited to testing."

After running SCP-XXXX for exactly 15 minutes, SCP-XXXX must be shut off immediately, and must not be interacted with for 35 minutes after use.

This is worded non-clinically and sounds out of place as a result. Additionally, it leaves the question of "what do we do if it's left on for longer?". Try "Should SCP-XXXX remain in an active state for longer than 15 minutes […]".

After removing and opening the storage compartment of SCP-XXXX, Class A personnel and higher may remove the contents of the bag. Failure to comply with these guidelines will lead to swift termination.

Again, clinical tone. Try "Removal of SCP-XXXX's storage compartment and its contents is restricted to assigned personnel with Class A clearance."

If SCP-XXXX is interacted with too quickly between uses, SCP-XXXX will teleport the violator to an unknown dimension, presumably the origin of the items SCP-XXXX produces.

This is not a containment procedure and does not belong here. Now onto the description:

SCP-XXXX resembles a pre-owned Oreck Vacuum Cleaner, about 1 meter high when assembled

Does the object resemble a vacuum cleaner, or is it a vacuum cleaner? If it's a man who shape-shifted into a vacuum, then it would "resemble" one. If it's a vacuum with anomalous powers, however, it's still a vacuum. Also, you don't need to state the height of the object unless it's significant to its anomalous properties.

When plugged into a standard American power outlet, SCP-XXXX will begin to emit a loud suction sound, comparable to any other vacuum.

You don't need to state this. In other words, you've said "When it's plugged in, the vacuum will make sounds like a vacuum." Remove it.

When used, SCP-XXXX will not remove any dirt, grime or debris from the ground, but will seem to pull from other dimensions.

Again, the wording here is weird. "When used" how? "will seem to pull" what "from other dimensions"? Assuming you meant matter, how has the Foundation confirmed this is where it originates from. How do they know the object is not manifesting matter instead? How do they know the matter is from another dimension instead of just a distant location in this one?

Previous testing's of SCP-XXXX have yielded:

This sentence is worded poorly. "Testing with SCP-XXXX has provided inconsistent results." would work better. I would also consider expanding on the narrative here since there really isn't one elsewhere. If the vacuum "steals" matter from other locations, what are the consequences in those locations?

Addendum:

I'll admit that I skimmed through this as it just didn't seem that interesting. The addendum adds nothing we didn't already know and only raises more questions than it answers.

In short, I think the basic idea of the object is interesting and can go somewhere. The draft, in the current state it's in now, needs a lot of revision. I think you need to focus on developed a central narrative / story for this because as it stands currently, it's just an anomalous item.

As the containment of SCP-001 requires an incomplete understanding of its purpose, parameters, and function, the Classification Committee has voted to establish the Atelis object class. item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
I will not pretend that this article is any sort of pioneering effort into the world of philosophy in SCPs, but rather it represents my sincere and personal wish for all of us, myself included, to continue to seek balance and to challenge our preconceptions. We must learn to find The Middle Way and walk the liminal path between the order and chaos of the world around us.

There are many aspects of this piece I have chosen not to comment on and clarify in this post. This is not to say that I would not talk about them but rather I think the piece as a whole is better served by being left open-ended. I am eager to see how the journey is perceived by those with other perspectives.

Thank you for all of your readership in the two years I have been posting my works to the wiki. I have so much more I want to share and I only now feel as if I have learned how to walk in between the legs of these literary giants that I am privileged to share the space with. This is the most important thing I have ever written and I couldnt feel better about taking the risk to share it with you.

An special thank you to users LordStonefish , plaidypus, Quadraginta, and Dysadron who all provided critical feedback on the finished draft and helped me realize a much more rounded final product. An additional thanks to MalyceGraves for their help in brainstorming for the long game over the many months it took me to arrive to this destination.

LITERARY ATTRIBUTIONS
Thank you

The quote, "Church is a hospital for sinners", is attributed to St. Augustine of Hippo, John Chrysostom, and Abigail Van Buren, among others.

The quote "They shall beat their swords to plowshares" is Biblical, Isaiah 2:3-4

To start I want to thank you for spending the time to review my SCP, it means a great deal to me, I want to also apologize beforehand because it's very difficult to convey my thoughts in general and my ADD doesn't help that.

So to start I am teetering on whether I should make this a tale or an article. The way I have currently planned this was so that I start out that the ship is the SCP it has crashed and is the Foundations initial item of focus. But then they become aware of an alarming amount of radiation beginning to leak from the ship. Now I choose the Serpent's Hand initially because they seemed to be the most likely to be the ones who'd help him infiltrate the Foundation. The bomb is what's producing the radiation and acts as the reason as to why the alien came to the Solas system.

I'm also beginning to agree with you on the matter of not taking on a humanoid SCP. My goal with this is to convey the story of a man trapped and cut off from the ones he loves and to convey the heartwrenching agony he goes through as he comes to terms with that realization. He is also only visually similar, such as his face, but he as other organs, in the article I was planning to have the Foundation find the dead members of his crew and then have a list of their biological differences in an autopsy report.

The way I want to tell this is through personnel logs, starting after he leaves his homeworld, then proceeding up till the point they get the bomb and crash on Earth and such. The grammar issues are definitely mounting I agree I've been having difficulty addressing them in general, and grammar has always been an issue for me, I use Grammarly to help but there is only so much it's able to do of course.

Again thank you for your feedback, it honestly brings me a great deal of excitement to receive it, and pride that I've be noticed even if my SCP isn't very good. So thank you again for your help, and have a good holiday.

item.title: Re: Seeking out greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Central Narrative: none

If you are not planning on having any sort of narrative at all, then this really doesn't belong outside of the log of anomalous items. Actually, it might not even belong there, because I don't think you even know what it is. You just say that it is "an SCP", but… What does that mean? Is it a rock? A ferret?

You should be focusing less on what connections people might potentially make between your idea and 173 and more on what your actual idea is. Right now, you have an anomalous occurrence with no object and also no apparent plans to give your article a narrative. This is not nearly even close to qualifying for a greenlight.

To get you started with brainstorming, you might want to consider:

  • Why is this object what it is (once you decide what you're writing about)?
  • Did someone make it? If so, why?
  • How did the Foundation acquire it?
  • You say it is "harder to contain whenever it escapes". Why is this? Is it just because it disrupts electrical containment methods? Is there some reason why the Foundation cannot contain it without electricity?
  • Why does light immobilize it? Does the type of light (UV, infrared, etc.) matter? Why?

item.title: Re: Out of One Voice (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Hey! First of all, big thank for the response and crit.

My response to your response
Howdy

I'm not completely sold on the idea of DMV "winning" necessarily…

I agree with you. I had one big idea I was unsure of, but that pesky 400 word limit (Yeah, I get why it's there but still) forced my hand to cut the revision notes short. As we've learned with many many Articles and tales, rarely does something "good" happen to the Foundation without consequences.

The phrase Voce de Voci comes to mind for a hypothetical takeover by 035.

Voce de Voci really appeals to me, and I'm going to write that down, so thank you for that. Now a takeover is along the lines of my idea. Though not for 035 actively trying. The very act of Di Molte Voci containing an entity that gave voices to everything, well… that alters what exactly DMV considers consensus.

When you get down to it, words and voices are consensus based. We collectively decide that dog means dog, mask means mask, and run means run. it's an agreement. Considering The Voice is the ultimate authority (or was in any case) over voices. that's both covered.

The way that Scranton describes it, money (being a very large combination of consensus and authority) can not be used in relation to DMV. So…

I wouldn't be surprised by a second memo regarding the documentation of Di Molte Voci being to slowly degrade and/or corrode over time.

Here in comes the alteration to Di Molte Voci. DMV now actively prevents the use of voice around it. As it continues to alter and shift, with 035's corrosion effect translating into a breakdown of the "game" that DMV plays.

The implications of things done by 035 being reversed (i.e. the corrosion reverted and damage being healed) becomes a problem. If we consider this take on 035/The Voice to have given voices to all, and that action reverting, then we have a world eventually without voice. With the only authority over voices, being Di Molte Voci.


Maybe too heavy handed for a first time article but hey, it's an idea.
Again thank you for your crit! Have a good day/night now. I require sleep.

item.title: Re: SCP-something: Man unable to communicate properly
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the advice! The food for thought was very nutritious.
I completely agree that there were some unnecessary redactions, and I've removed the extraneous ones.
I never meant to give the impression that the Foundation was hostile towards SCPxx, only that Dr Adam Pink was. I've made a few adjustments to make that point clearer.
As for the ending, I'll agree that there are several rather unconnected threads, and that there is no clear conclusion to the story. However (and I may be blaspheming with this statement), is that such a bad thing? My goal with the article is for the reader to feel drawn into the mystery, and to feel a level of compassion for the SCP. I think most of the article does a reasonable job of fostering that. The sideline with the missing husband, in my opinion, is reasonably unsettling if nothing else.
I should also mention that one of my goals for the article was to write it in such a way that the SCP might not be anomalous at all.
In any case, I don't doubt that I'll be making adjustments to the article for a while yet. Thank you for looking at it!

item.title: Re: Out of One Voice (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
For starters I really like the core idea you've got here- the idea of these two masks as opposing forces with a deeper connection is a very cool and natural-feeling concept.

That said, I'm not completely sold on the idea of DMV "winning" necessarily…we've seen globally in recent years what happens when consensus reality intersects with persuasive liars; the results aren't pretty. The phrase Voce de Voci comes to mind for a hypothetical takeover by 035. At the same time, if you read between the lines, 035 is driven in large part by its own existential fear, so I think you've got the reaction right if it found itself losing the fight for control, and a good visual for what that could look like.

Where the real danger enters is that whether 035 escapes intact or is neutralized, I wouldn't be surprised by a second memo regarding the documentation of Di Molte Voci being to slowly degrade and/or corrode over time.

item.title: Re: Elbows
item.content:encoded:
My attempt to answer your concerns:

So like any person who is "not normal" experiences to some degree, this person was bullied or mocked at some point in their life. Being mocked for "weird arms" would have potentially led to a retort something to the effect of "maybe you have weird arms!" Whether it was voiced or not.

Something (and exploring exactly what that something is may provide more/additional narrative value than what I have here in my response) has happened to make that retort, that idea that the person with "normal arms" is in fact the person with "weird arms" believed by any person who physically interacts with the SCP, even if they interacted in the nicest way with the best of intentions. Justice has "gone awry" in that it's not only affecting people who mock or bully the subject, it's affecting everyone.

Something else that I have in my mind but maybe should have included in the concept is that the anomalous property emerged in adulthood, largely past the kind of overt bullying that might have made something like this slightly more appealing. So it's gone awry in that it's both too intense, and well past the time that it would have been even remotely desirable.

I don't know if that solves the problems by itself or simply over-explains the concept, but there is my response.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
1) It's generally assumed that if your soul is used for the basis of an SCP that you died at some point. Otherwise, it can get rather awkward.

You really can't assume anything with anomalies. There are a number of items in the archives that involve this sort of thing, and it does indeed get awkward. That is a good thing for narrative purposes. SCP-3009 for instance revolves around a situation where the Foundation can't figure out whether one, both, or neither of a pair are the original person. There are anomalies that involve things like ambiguous duplication of a person obliviously living an otherwise normal life elsewhere, and others where it's implied that the anomaly involves an afterimage or reflection of a person and their desires at a certain moment in their lives.

The fact that this is a Philosophy student opens up some really cool opportunities on that front that I'd HIGHLY recommend embracing and running with. The meaning of "self" when we all shed identities over time, the search for truth and meaning, what constitutes a fulfilling life, whether there's any real value in contemplating paths not taken… These are are all long-standing philosophical topics that get extremely relevant to this anomaly if in 1989 Charles Anton Page changed his major from philosophy to business and is currently employed as a Junior Partner at a minor accounting firm in Oakland.

item.title: The Phantom
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Class, containment procedures, a professional description of the SCP and what it does, followed by three incident reports.

Elevator Pitch: Put simply, SCP-XXXX is a cat-like apparition which consumes souls. It once had intangibility (Which it lost during an incident), and it can shield itself from all wavelengths of light, rendering itself invisible for a short duration.

It’s a hunter, so it stalks any kind of prey which catches its interest, though it prefers humans. It will stalk its target, memorizing all of its routines, mannerisms, and daily patterns in extreme detail. When they are at a point of vulnerability (Provided SCP-XXXX hasn’t lost interest) it will consume their soul.

After a large amount of souls are consumed, it exhales them into the form of a polychromatic sphere, which it then carries to an unidentifiable and unspecified location.

That’s how it’s going to be written, but in actuality, SCP-XXXX is bringing the sphere to a GOI (Of my creation) so they can use it to prevent some kind of cataclysmic event from occurring. The Foundation is unaware of this, and all they know is that whenever they try to take the sphere away from the SCP, several events occur:

  1. SCP-XXXX becomes extremely agitated.
  2. People start disappearing from the Foundation (They’re actually being dragged away by a hand of the SCP which actually causes the cataclysmic event.)
  3. Emergence of multiple anomalous entities appearing all over the world.
  4. Cataclysmic event occurs.

Central Narrative: It’s a question of morals. The Foundation has to escort SCP outside after it creates the sphere (Which can even be a problem at times), but each time it’s outside it also does what it wants, and consumes even more souls. Even though the SCP’s job is presumably important, is it morally correct for the Foundation to just let it go around killing people?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Since the SCP has lost its intangibility and is now at odds with the Foundation, this prompts it to use its superior intelligence to resist and counteract any new containment procedures that the Foundation tries to come up with.

Additional Notes: Last time I left out a lot of details, since I was trying to summarize way too much. Hopefully this is a good balance of things. Once again, any advice is highly appreciated, and thanks in advance.
